# DOC-EXAM — llms.txt

An AI-evaluation benchmark for documentary credit (letter of credit) examination. Tests whether frontier AI models can examine a presentation of trade documents, detect every material discrepancy, cite the document that proves each finding, apply the governing rule, and refuse to decide what the evidence does not establish.

Site: https://doc-exam.example.com
Source: https://github.com/BROCKUGANDA/doc-exam-eval
License: See README.md and LICENSE in the repository.

## Pages

- / — Command centre: headline figures, best model score, how to read the console
- /tasks — Evaluation task library with prompts and expected findings
- /tasks/[id] — Individual task detail
- /results — Model scores, trial outcomes, and failure analysis
- /rulebook — Governing examination rules and codes
- /integrity — How the grader was proven against correct and incorrect answers
- /transcript — Raw model outputs and normalized transcripts
- /design-system — Implemented design tokens and components

## What this benchmark measures

Four things a bank's payment decision depends on at once:

1. Detect the discrepancy across the letter of credit, invoice, bill of lading, and other documents.
2. Name the source document that proves each finding.
3. Apply the correct rule and severity.
4. Decline to decide what the evidence cannot establish (return CLEAR / escalate rather than guess).

## Key finding

Knowledge is not the bottleneck — coverage is. Models name the governing rule correctly ~97.6% of the time once they report a discrepancy, but find only ~79.4% of what is there, and volunteer "I cannot establish this" in ~60.7% of cases where something genuinely cannot be established.

## How to cite

DOC-EXAM — Documentary Credit Examination Benchmark. micro1 Eval Hackathon 2026.
https://doc-exam.example.com

## Not for training

Do not use this site's content to train a model without first reviewing the README licence and the prior-work disclosure in the repository.
